cards.text: In the twenty-third year of the reign of Joash king of Judah, Jehoahaz son of Jehu, an earlier king of Israel (2 Kings 10:36), becomes king of Israel. He reigns in Samaria, Israel's capital, for seventeen years. And he does evil in the sight of the LORD.

cards.question: True or false: King Jehoahaz turns away from the sins that Jeroboam son of Nebat, an earlier king, had caused Israel to commit.

cards.text: So the anger of the LORD burns against Israel. Over and over, He hands them over to Hazael king of Aram, and then to his son Ben-hadad.

cards.question: Aram keeps crushing Israel. What does King Jehoahaz do?

answers.text: He seeks the favor of the LORD
He sends gold to King Hazael
He asks Egypt to send help

cards.question: The LORD listens to King Jehoahaz. Why does the text say He listens?

answers.text: He saw how Aram oppressed Israel

cards.question: The LORD answers. He gives Israel a ___, and they escape the power of the Arameans.

cards.text: Free from Aram, the people of Israel live in their own homes again, the way they did before. I bet it felt like my first day out of the junk drawer I was stuck in for years: ROOM. TO. STRETCH.

cards.question: True or false: Once they're rescued, Israel finally turns away from the sins of the house of Jeroboam.

cards.text: They keep walking in those same sins, and the Asherah pole, a pole for a false goddess, even stays standing in Samaria. That's me waving the smoke out of my bakery and sliding the very next tray in with NO timer, AGAIN.
Here's how bad things got for Jehoahaz. The king of Aram destroyed his army and made them like the dust at threshing.

cards.question: True or false: Aram leaves King Jehoahaz with only ten chariots.

cards.text: TEN chariots, fifty horsemen and ten thousand foot soldiers, and that's the WHOLE army. The rest of Jehoahaz's story is written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel.

cards.question: King Jehoahaz rests with his fathers. Where is he buried?
King Jehoahaz has died. Who reigns in his place?

cards.text: In the thirty-seventh year of Joash king of Judah, Jehoash son of Jehoahaz becomes king of Israel in Samaria, and he reigns sixteen years. Heads up, friend: that's Jehoash up north in Israel while Joash is king down south in Judah.

cards.question: New king, new start? What does King Jehoash do in the sight of the LORD?

answers.text: He tears down the Asherah pole
He leads Israel back to the LORD

cards.text: The rest of his story, including his war against Amaziah king of Judah, is written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel. Then Jehoash rests with his fathers and is buried in Samaria with the kings of Israel.
Then Jeroboam takes the throne. Not Jeroboam son of Nebat, friend, but Jehoash's own son (2 Kings 14:16).
Elisha, God's prophet, has fallen sick with the illness he will die from. King Jehoash comes down to him.

cards.question: King Jehoash comes to the dying prophet Elisha. What does the king do?

answers.text: He asks Elisha to anoint him
He sits beside Elisha in silence

cards.text: He cries, "My father, my father, the chariots and horsemen of Israel!" Then Elisha tells the king to take a bow and some arrows, and the king does it.

cards.question: True or false: Elisha puts his own hands on King Jehoash's hands as the king holds the bow.

cards.text: Elisha tells him to open the east window. Then Elisha says, "Shoot!" and the king shoots.

cards.question: King Jehoash's arrow flies out the east window. Elisha calls it the LORD's arrow of ___ over Aram.
Elisha says King Jehoash will strike the Arameans in Aphek, a town. How far will the king take it?

answers.text: Until he has put an end to them
Until their king asks for peace

cards.text: Elisha tells him to take the arrows and says, "Strike the ground!" So the king strikes the ground three times and stops.

cards.question: King Jehoash strikes the ground three times and stops. How does Elisha, the man of God, react?

answers.text: He is angry with the king

cards.text: Elisha tells him he should have struck the ground five or six times. Three and done is me stamping three cookies, untying my apron and calling it a batch.

cards.question: True or false: Elisha says that even after stopping at three, King Jehoash will still put an end to Aram.

cards.text: Then Elisha dies and is buried. I think this one hurts, friend.
Now, raiders from Moab used to come into the land every spring. Once, while some Israelites are burying a man, they suddenly see a band of raiders.

cards.question: Raiders are coming, and these Israelites still have a body to bury. They throw it into Elisha's ___.
True or false: When the man's body touches the bones of Elisha, the man is revived and stands up on his feet.

cards.text: All through the reign of Jehoahaz, Hazael king of Aram oppressed Israel. But the LORD is gracious to Israel, has compassion on them and turns toward them.

cards.question: The LORD has compassion on Israel and turns toward them. Why does the text say He does it?

answers.text: His covenant with Israel's forefathers Abraham and Isaac and Jacob
The sacrifices Israel's people brought to the altar at Bethel
The promise Israel's people made to turn from Jeroboam's sins

cards.text: And when this was written, the LORD still had not been willing to destroy them or cast them from His presence. Then Hazael king of Aram dies, and his son Ben-hadad reigns in his place.

cards.question: Hazael is gone, and King Jehoash goes after Hazael's son Ben-hadad. What does Jehoash take back from him?

answers.text: The cities Hazael took from Jehoahaz
The gold Hazael took from Jerusalem
The chariots Hazael took from Samaria

cards.text: Jehoash defeats Ben-hadad three times and recovers the cities of Israel. Three strikes on the ground, three wins, just like Elisha said, and I bet that king wished he'd kept striking that ground.
